summary: The independent review counterexample was reproduced at the exact candidate commit: after a libc printf before importing FlyDSL, READY arrived while the child was alive with only PREIMPORT readable, and all four synchronized device lines remained buffered until exit. The candidate's valid import-time stdout configuration and explicit flush helper were preserved, but stdout is now made unbuffered rather than line buffered. On the prepared glibc environment this remains effective after the pre-import C stdio write. A timing-independent GPU regression covers the counterexample and verifies all four thread IDs before teardown.

tests.what_was_measured: Failing-before timing evidence: at READY while the child was alive, stdout was exactly PREIMPORT; all four device lines became readable only after child exit. Raw output: reports/j-6ff0a8515a2c/raw/before-review-counterexample.log.
Passing-after timing evidence: PREIMPORT and exactly four device thread lines were readable at READY while the child remained alive, with no additional stdout at teardown.

All five GPU pipe cases passed, including the exact pre-import libc-write counterexample, one and three launches, and explicit-flush compatibility. Each checks visibility while the child is alive and exact thread IDs.
All 15 focused runtime and printf-lowering unit tests passed.
A real gfx950 vector addition matched the independent PyTorch a+b reference with maximum error 0.00e+00 over 1,048,576 float32 elements.

gpu_execution.evidence: One assigned AMD Instinct MI355X with gfx950 capability ran the failing-before candidate reproduction, passing-after counterexample, five-case pipe regression, and independent numerical vector-add check.

remaining_limitations: Validation was limited to Linux/glibc 2.39, ROCm 7.2, and one MI355X/gfx950; an actual Jupyter frontend and other libc/GPU architectures were unavailable.
Changing C stdout buffering is process-wide and affects other C/C++ stdout writers after FlyDSL import.

No C++ or LLVM source changed, so the prescribed native rebuild was not applicable. Python sources loaded from /job/repo/python/flydsl and native bindings remained supplied by /opt/venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/flydsl/_mlir.
The prepared Python environment did not include ruff, so formatting was checked with git diff --check and explicit line-length inspection rather than the ruff command.
